chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever memorizes forty hadiths from our hadiths, God will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection as a scholar and a jurist.

key_terms.أَحَادِيثِنَا: Our hadiths — the traditions attributed to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ: Forty — a significant number in Islamic tradition, evoking completeness and devotion
key_terms.حَفِظَ: To memorize/preserve — here referring to committed retention and transmission of hadith
key_terms.عَالِماً: Scholar — one who possesses formal religious knowledge
key_terms.فَقِيهاً: Jurist — one who has deep comprehension and understanding of Islamic law and theology

ai.seo_question: What reward is promised for memorizing forty hadiths in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) promises a great spiritual reward for those who memorize forty hadiths from the Imams' traditions: they will be raised on the Day of Judgment as learned scholars and jurists. This hadith reflects the early Islamic tradition of honoring and transmitting the sayings of the Imams, and is part of a broader category of forty-hadith traditions found across both Sunni and Shia literature. The term 'faqih' (jurist) emphasizes not mere memorization, but the attainment of deep understanding and the ability to derive legal and ethical guidance.
